## The problem
<!-- 
  Describe the issue you are experiencing here to communicate to the
  maintainers. Tell us what you were trying to do and what happened.
-->
I have a thermostat connected to the Tuya platform integrated to my Home Assistant. During the configuration I had to set parameters Temperature values divider and Current temperature value divider to "10". I can see current temperature on my Dashboard (see attached screenshot). However in case I will try to change the target temperature (via moving the the slider), the current temperature disappears and title "Unavailable" is displayed for some time (probably until next state refresh from device). After some period, the current temperature is displayed again. But the target temperature is not set on thermostat. In the history I can see "Became unavailable by service climate.set_temperature".

I have written a simple script to set the target temperature via script.

```
termostat26:
  alias: TERMOSTAT 26
  sequence:
  - service: climate.set_temperature
    data:
      entity_id: climate.501170138caab5ebe016
      temperature: 26

```

But the result is the same (tried to set temperature to 26 and 260). After calling the script, the device became Unavailable for a while and target temperature is not set.

Setting target temperature via native Tuya mobile app or directly on device works OK.

No errors or warnings are displayed in Home Assistant log.

## Environment
<!--
  Provide details about the versions you are using, which helps us to reproduce
  and find the issue quicker. Version information is found in the
  Home Assistant frontend: Configuration -> Info.
-->

- Home Assistant Core release with the issue: 0.118.4
- Last working Home Assistant Core release (if known): N/A
- Operating environment (OS/Container/Supervised/Core): Raspberry Pi (HassOS 4.17)
- Integration causing this issue: Tuya
- Link to integration documentation on our website: https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/tuya/

## Problem-relevant `configuration.yaml`
<!--
  An example configuration that caused the problem for you. Fill this out even
  if it seems unimportant to you. Please be sure to remove personal information
  like passwords, private URLs and other credentials.
-->

```yaml

```

<!--
  If you come across any trace or error logs, please provide them.
-->

No errors are produced in any Home Assistant log.

review_comments: This test won't work in isolation since the config flow module won't be loaded unless the integration is tried to set up at least once. I'd set up the integration and then unload it and then test this.
I will create a followup PR for this, but can you provide me an example / reference on how to implement your request?

Something like this:
```py
# Set up the integration to make sure the config flow module is loaded.
assert await hass.config_entries.async_setup(config_entry.entry_id)
await hass.async_block_till_done()
# Unload the integration to prepare for the test.
assert await hass.config_entries.async_unload(config_entry.entry_id)
await hass.async_block_till_done()
# Start the test.
result = await hass.config_entries.options.async_init(config_entry.entry_id)
```
If the default is true, do we need to migrate the config entry to version 2 so all the existing users get the change?

Because the temperature provided by the device could be divided inside the library by the value set by the previous options `TEMP_DIVIDER`, this parameter instruct the library in the `set_temperature` method if to use this divider also for the set command. A parameter is required because different devices have different behavior and there is no way to determinate automatically the correct one. Using value `True` or `False` as default is just a choice, `True` seems more logic because is using in the set temperature command the same value returned as target temperature.
Default = True is also managed in the climate class, so I don't think is required to migrate config entry to a new version. If option is not available is set to `True`.

I explained with an example here to be more clear.

Suppose that the device report for target temperature  the value 210. 
Setting `divider` to 10 in the library, target temperature returned by tuyaha will became 21.0.

If now I send a `set_temperature` command to the library with value 22.0, I have 2 option:
- case 1, `use_divider = true` -> `set_temperature` will send to the device value 22.0
- case 2, `use_divider = false` -> `set_temperature` will send to the device value 220
Please add a test to the options flow for the new options
